question: Should OpenClaw enforce this repository-specific publication policy through the installed pre-push lifecycle, or keep it as voluntary contributor guidance instead of merging a fail-closed guard that is bypassed by ordinary `git push`?
rationale: The correct enforcement point changes contributor workflow and determines whether this is security control or optional hygiene; source evidence cannot make that policy choice.

options.title: Install and enforce the guard
options.body: Wire the checker into the repository-owned pre-push hook, retain existing hook work, and add end-to-end hook proof for unsafe and safe push cases.

options.title: Keep it advisory
options.body: Retain only documentation and a manual command, but remove fail-closed security claims and treat it as optional local hygiene.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Close or defer the branch if maintainers do not want repository-specific remote and path policy in contributor workflows.

recommendation.title: Install and enforce the guard
recommendation.body: Wire the checker into the repository-owned pre-push hook, retain existing hook work, and add end-to-end hook proof for unsafe and safe push cases.
